text:
maria.r: FYI I noticed a steady mem growth on kv-cache over a 48h window for long-context traffic (seq len ~12k). Heap snaps + allocator traces look like free-list fragmentation + lots of tiny holes that don't get reused.

ajay.k: what metrics / snapshots do you have?

maria.r: Pasted allocator summary (from /sys/kvcache/stats) — quick snippet:
```
alloc_total: 92.3GB
free_small: 4.6GB
free_large: 1.1GB
external_frag_pct: 18.7
avg_block: 92KB
active_chunks: 3124
long_context_resident: 28GB
```
Also a pprof heap diff shows ~2.4GB growth correlated with requests that keep KV windows open.

taylor: external_frag_pct ~19% is pretty high. Did something change in kernel selection or kv chunk sizing recently?

maria.r: We rolled out a kernel selection tweak last week that biases certain backends toward smaller compute kernels, but it also unintentionally bumped the default per-token kv chunk in the runtime from 64KB -> 128KB for some pools. My hypothesis: larger chunk granularity makes reuse harder for long tails, increasing fragmentation.

ben: that matches a signal I saw in staging — bigger chunks reduce per-token overhead but worsen fragmentation for mixed-length workloads.

perf-bot: uploaded profile: https://perf.redwood/trace/1764823333-kv-frag (contains trace, heap diffs, alloc histograms)

ajay.k: Can we try reducing block size back to 64KB for the affected pool and run a compaction probe?

maria.r: I ran a short A/B on a single pod: 128KB->64KB reduced external_frag from 19% -> 9% over 6h but CPU jitter increased ~3%. Quick numbers:
```
before: ext_frag 19.1%  cpu 62%
after:  ext_frag 9.3%   cpu 65%
```
So it's a CPU vs mem tradeoff.

taylor: Instead of reverting globally, propose a background compaction signal that targets cold slabs when fragmentation crosses a threshold. Example trigger: when free_ratio < 12% AND ext_frag_pct > 12% AND long_context_resident > 10GB, kick compaction for least-recently-used slabs at a rate cap.

ben: sounds reasonable. Need to ensure compaction is cooperative so it doesn't stall inference. Maybe a controlled mover that yields between KV page relocations and respects in-flight KV windows.

maria.r: Sketch of kvctl command for canary run:
```
kvctl compact --selector pool=seq-mixed --budget 40MB/s --mode cooperative --trigger "ext_frag>12 and free_ratio<12"
```
We'll emit metrics: `kv.compaction.bytes_moved`, `kv.compaction.active_seconds`, `kv.eviction.unexpected`.

ajay.k: Also add a reuse_distance histogram per-pool; that helps tune block_size and compaction aggressiveness. If median reuse_distance >> block_size, compaction will help.

taylor: timeline?

maria.r: I'll spin a canary today: 3 pods in staging with cooperative compaction + 64KB block override, run for 24h, collect ext_frag, cpu, p95/p99, and reuse_distance. If we see ext_frag drop ~>8-10% with tail latency within 1% we'll plan a gradual rollout to the prod pool next week.

ben: please add an SRE runbook snippet for rollback: how to disable compaction and revert block-size (one-liner flags + TL;DR steps).

maria.r: will add runbook and post results. :thumbsup: 

perf-bot: scheduled check-in alert in 24h (canary metrics will be posted to #eng-runtime).
